short_description: American Community Survey (ACS) contains base population data. It collects similar data to the census but is run every year, so it has more up to date data but is slightly less accurate due to being a survey rather than a census. We pull a selection of variables relating to demographics, insurance, education, poverty, veteran status, etc.. The same variables can be available at different geographic levels (for example, DemographicState5YR2023 is also available for county and census tract). The estimates can be obtained on different years, so the year is listed in the table name. As indicated on each table, we only obtained 5-year estimates although ACS provides other windows.

Area Deprivation Index (ADI) ranks neighborhoods by socioeconomic disadvantage (the higher the rank, the more disadvantaged) within each state and within the whole nation. We currently only have one table for ADI for 2022 at the geographic level of the census block group, but others could be obtained.

Annual Homeless Assessment Report (AHAR) reports homelessness across the US. It breaks down homelessness by many different factors. It's available at the state and national level for a few different years.

Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (BRFSS) contains health risk behaviors. The data we pull mainly covers cancer screening and tobacco usage. It's available For the nation, the AWS, and the state.

The US Census data covers demographic data. We pull a few variables from the 2020 census for some base population measures (age, race and ethnicity, etc.). It is preferred to use the ACS data when possible because it's more recent. Additionally, the census data has FIPS codes which are unique geographic identifiers for each state, county, census tract, and so on. This is a rare case where a table from this schema could be joined with a table from another schema if that table uses a FIPS code instead of a name.

Community Health Assessment Survey (CHAS) is a survey conducted by HCI. It's specifically focused on gathering data on frontier populations, so it should not be used in general scenarios when survey data it covers is requested. It should only be used either when a survey variable it contains is asked for in the context of frontier areas or if the variable asked for is only available in the CHAS data and no other dataset.

Cancer InFocus (CIF) is a broad dataset. It's built by another cancer center who has a similar database to SHAPE, so it contains a wide variety of data sources including cancer incidence and mortality, social determinants of health, behavioral and environmental risk factors, cancer screening, and many others.
Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has many data sources, but we only pull radon potential and air quality index (AQI).
Federal Communications Commission (FCC) provides data about broadband and mobile internet speeds. This gives us a proxy of people who can access telehealth.

Health Information National Trends Survey (HINTS) has similar data to BRFSS with the addition of information covering health perceptions and health communication. This survey is much smaller than BRFSS, so BRFSS is preferred when a variable is in both datasets.

Vaccination Coverage Among Adolescents (VCAA) is used for HPV vaccination data. This has data for many geographic levels, age ranges, and years but they are all contained in the single table. It was released in 2023, but it has historical data as well.

Integrated Metropolitan-to-Frontier Area Codes (IMFAC) classifies each census tract or county as metropolitan, micropolitan, noncore, or frontier. It is a new alternative to RUCA that is more expressive for areas like ours that have lots of frontier area. It uses FIPS codes, so it would need to be joined with another dataset to be interpretable.
Huntsman Cancer Institute (HCI). This schema has a single table listing the locations of HCI and its affiliates.

National Health Interview Survey (NHIS) contains survey data similar to HINTS and BRFSS. However, it does not have a geographic level more specific than census region, so it's the least preferred survey dataset.

Rural-Urban Commuting Area (RUCA) classifies each census tract or zip code as rural, urban, etc.. This has been the standard in the field, but we prefer to use IMFAC unless specified. It uses FIPS codes, so it would need to be joined with another dataset to be interpretable.
The rurality schema has one table that is the result of a research project to classify the rurality of census tracts. It is interesting, but typically IMFAC or RUCA is preferred.

Social Vulnerability Index (SVI) identifies communities vulnerable to public health crises. The overall index can be viewed, or one can look at more specific indexes giving interpretability to the overall index. It is available at the county, census tract, or zcta level.
Travel time (tt) schema contains travel time geometries around HCI and each of its affiliates. This can show on a map how long it might take for patients to access one of our facilities.
US Department of Agriculture (USDA) has many data sources, but we only pull their data on poverty. This is the preferred data source for poverty. It is available at the county and census tract level.
